Use the LOWER-FILL/MEDIUM-WIDE branch and retain the laptop at its initial position, slightly left of center in the lower-middle frame. Camera: Retain the laptop's exact visible screen, keyboard, chassis faces and perspective. Use a level camera slightly above seated eye height, looking gently downward, with a natural moderately wide room view and no roll. The laptop remains at its original pixel size and position. Construct the table and glass-walled room with consistent vanishing geometry around that view. Show the near working edge below the laptop, with open knee space and a pulled-back chair to the lower left; do not extend the tabletop into the user's seating space.

Composition: The unchanged laptop occupies the lower-middle, slightly left of center, facing the near-camera working edge. Furniture scale assumes a typical compact laptop rather than treating its projected width as a physical measurement. The sturdy pale oak table provides full base support, natural contact shadow, generous rear and side clearance, and unobstructed keyboard access. In the middle plane at right, place exactly two unlabelled architectural finish samples—a small oak veneer board and a light limestone tile—flat beside each other on the table, within reach and each smaller than the keyboard deck. A palm-sized gray stone paperweight rests beside them, slightly farther from the working edge. A ribbed-glass divider stands on the floor in the far-left background. A slate blue felt privacy screen stands on the floor in the far-right background, its broad panel filling much of the upper-right area. Clear glass office walls span the distant background. A neutral upholstered working chair is pulled back toward the lower left, partly cropped, facing the laptop without overlapping it. Cool, even daylight enters from the left with generous fill and gentle reflections. No requested object is omitted and no request conflicts with the product or no-person restriction.

TRANSLATION-ONLY PRODUCT PLACEMENT; RECOMPOSED SUPPORT
